name: focal-point-field
title: Focal point field
description: Mark the part of an image that must never be cropped: click or drag a point and see square, wide and tall crops that keep it in view.
docs: The image carries a crosshair handle that works like a two-axis slider: click or drag anywhere on the picture, or focus the handle and use the arrow keys (1%, Shift 10%) and Home to centre it. step is the unit in percent: the point snaps to its multiples and the keys move by it, Shift by ten times as much. The handle is role slider and says its place as 45% across, 30% down (labels.position). Beside the image, previews (default square, wide 16:9 and tall 3:4; pass your own { label, ratio } list) show the same picture cropped with object-position set to the point, side by side at one height (a row that is full wraps to the next, and a very narrow shape keeps a width a crop can be judged at), so the result is seen before saving. onValueChange reports { x, y } as numbers from 0 to 100, ready for object-position: ${x}% ${y}%; value and defaultValue control it. Pointer events make it work with mouse, touch and pen, and a handle grabbed by its edge does not jump to the pointer. The image is shown as large as fits in 26rem of height; while it loads there is a skeleton, and an image that fails shows a calm error with the reason and a Try again button. name submits the point as nameX and nameY. labels carries every word.
